title: Launch readiness
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for deciding whether a site or app is ready to launch: every link resolved, every status claim matched against a live check, the analytics statement compared with the requests the pages make, error pages, a rollback plan and the owner's go or no-go, while the release itself stays with a person.
boundaries: Every check is read-only; nothing on the site or its host is changed, submitted or signed into.
The owner decides and grants waivers; the release itself is a person's separate act.
A failed item stays on the record; its fix gets its own check.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for deciding whether a site or app is ready to launch

value.lets_workers: Plan a readiness check for one launch, resolve every link on the rendered pages, check every status claim against a live read or a receipt, compare the analytics statement with the requests the pages make, check error pages, review the rollback plan, assemble one report whose recommendation follows a fixed rule, and keep the owner's go or no-go as a noun. The release itself stays with a person.

flow.when: When a launch date or a public link is being decided.
On the rendered pages; deterministic and read-only.
For every status claim on the pages.
On page loads; deterministic and read-only.
With made-up addresses; deterministic and read-only.
When the parts are in; deterministic.
The owner decides; a person's verb.

guardrails: Every check is read-only: no form is submitted, no account is created and nothing is changed on the site or its host.
A status claim is matched against a live read or a receipt, never against memory or another page's words.
No analytics is a claim like any other: the page-load requests must agree with it.
The recommendation follows from the items by a fixed rule; the owner decides, and the release itself is a separate act by a person.
complements: The release and verify pack proves a release went live correctly; this pack decides whether to launch at all.
Link checks reuse the rename and relink pack's link rules and link check shape.
Claims reuse the status and handoff pack's evidence rules.

nouns.title: How a launch readiness check runs, up to the owner's decision
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: plan-readiness names the target, the pages, the claims to check, the rollback target and who decides.
The check verbs each cover one checklist item, read-only.
assemble-readiness puts the items in one report and derives the recommendation.
record-go-decision: the owner records go, no_go or go_with_waivers on that exact report.
The release is the release owner's act, recorded with the release and verify pack.

recommendation_rule.not_ready: Any required item fails or is not checked, other than owner-go.
recommendation_rule.ready_with_waivers: No required item fails, and at least one is waived by the owner with a reason.
recommendation_rule.ready: Every required item except owner-go passes.

rules: A waiver is the owner's, with a reason; a worker never waives an item.
A failed item stays on the record when it is fixed; the fix gets its own check.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

nouns.title: The launch readiness checklist
nouns.category_reason: A fixed checklist every launch is checked against.

items.what: Every link on every page in scope resolves, and every in-page anchor exists.
items.evidence: A link check in the rename and relink pack's shape, run on the rendered pages.
items.pass: No broken links; every redirect is recorded with its final address; links that need sign-in are labeled as such on the page.

items.what: Every status claim on the pages, such as a count, a date, a version, live, measured or synthetic only, matches a live read-only check or a receipt.
items.pass: No claim is contradicted; unverifiable claims are reworded or waived by the owner.

items.what: The site says whether it uses analytics, and the network requests on page load match what it says.
items.pass: A statement exists and the observed requests agree with it; third parties are listed.

items.what: Unknown addresses return a 404 status with a helpful page and a way home; machine endpoints return errors with the right status.
items.pass: No soft 404s: a not-found page never answers 200.

items.what: The version to go back to, the steps, who can do it and how long it takes are written down before launch.
items.pass: All four are named and the target version exists.

items.what: A person's acceptance sign-off and an accessibility audit report are pinned, or the owner waives the gap with a reason.
items.evidence: Pins of a sign-off from the user acceptance testing pack and an audit report from the accessibility audit pack.
items.pass: The sign-off is go or go_with_conditions and the audit's P0 and P1 failures are fixed or waived.

items.what: The owner records go or no-go on this exact readiness report.
items.pass: A person's decision pinned to the report. The release itself is a separate act by a person.

items.what: Each page has a title, a description and its language set.
items.evidence: The structure lint from the accessibility audit pack.
items.pass: No page lacks a title or language.

items.what: A way to get help or report a problem is visible on every page.
items.pass: Help appears in the same place on every page.

value.rule: Required items decide the recommendation; optional items are reported and can be waived without a reason.

nouns.title: Finding and checking status claims on pages
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule for which claims to check and how.

claim_kinds.count: A number of things, such as packs, volunteers or tests. Check it against the source at a dated read.
claim_kinds.state: Words like live, deployed, measured, verified, reviewed or synthetic only. Check them with the evidence rules.
claim_kinds.version_or_date: A version, commit or as-of date. Check it is the current one, or that the page says as of when.
claim_kinds.capability: Something the product does, such as works with any agent. Check one real instance, or reword it as a goal.
claim_kinds.absence: Something the product does not do, such as no analytics or no AI calls. Check it with the matching read, such as page-load requests.

results.match: A live read or receipt says the same.
results.mismatch: A live read or receipt says otherwise; quote both.
results.unverifiable: No permitted read can check it; propose rewording it as dated or as a goal.

value.quote_exactly: Copy the claim's words exactly with where they appear, so the fix finds them.

nouns.title: Telling analytics requests from other third-party requests
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call classification rule with a starting list.

value.rule: A request is analytics when its host is listed here or a subdomain of one, or when it sends a page view or event beacon. Every other host that is not the site's own is a third party to list, with what it serves.
value.note: Font and script hosts are not analytics, but they still receive each visitor's address; list them so the privacy statement can mention them.
value.list_is_not_complete: The list is a starting point; record unknown third-party hosts for a person to classify.

nouns.title: What error pages must do
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule for error responses.

value.request: A made-up address under each surface, such as /this-page-does-not-exist-checked plus the date, with GET only.
expect: HTTP status 404 for a missing page; a not-found view that answers 200 is a soft 404 and fails
A helpful page in the site's own layout and language, with a link home
No stack trace, internal path or credential-shaped text
Machine endpoints answer a JSON error with the right status
value.single_page_apps: An app that renders every route in the browser still needs the server to answer 404 for unknown addresses; record both the status and the view.
value.server_errors: A 5xx page is checked only on a test target the owner named; otherwise record not_checked.

nouns.category_reason: Deterministic checks with synthetic known-good and known-bad records; the validator recomputes them.

verbs.title: Plan the readiness check
verbs.summary: Name the target and build, the pages, the status claims to check, the checklist items, the rollback target and the people who release and decide.
verbs.outcome: A readiness plan with every required checklist item.

slots.name: launch_brief
slots.description: Pin of a brief naming what launches, where, when and who decides.

steps: List every page people will reach from the launch link, and every status claim on them, quoted exactly.
Include every required checklist item, and say which optional ones apply.
Name the rollback target, the person who performs the release and the person who decides; an agent is never either.

acceptance.check: The plan validates against template.readiness-plan's schema.
items includes every required checklist item.
release_owner_role and decides_role name people's roles, not agents.
Every status claim on the pages is listed.

verbs.title: Check every link on the rendered pages
verbs.summary: Render each page in the plan, collect every link and in-page anchor, and resolve each with read-only requests, recording redirects, failures and links that need sign-in.
verbs.outcome: A link check in the rename and relink pack's shape.
steps: Collect links from the rendered pages, after scripts run, not only from the source files.
Request each absolute link read-only and record any redirect with its final address; check each in-page anchor against the ids on its page.
List links that land on a sign-in page under outside_control, so the page can say they need an account.

acceptance.check: The link check validates against the rename and relink pack's template.link-check schema.
ok plus redirected plus broken equals checked.
Every in-page anchor is checked against its page's ids.

network: Read-only page loads and GET requests to each link; no form is submitted and no sign-in is attempted.

verbs.title: Check every status claim on the pages
verbs.summary: Quote every status claim on the pages exactly and check each against a live read-only source or a pinned receipt, recording match, mismatch or unverifiable.
verbs.outcome: A page claims check, with a finding proposed for every mismatch.

slots.name: receipts
slots.description: Pins of receipts or check results the claims can be checked against, if any.

steps: Quote each claim exactly with the page it is on, and give it a claim kind from the claim rules.
Check each claim with the evidence the rules name, read now; never check a claim against another page's words or memory.
Mark a claim unverifiable when no permitted read can check it, and propose rewording it as dated or as a goal.
Propose findings-to-fixes.record-finding for every mismatch, quoting both the claim and the observed value.

acceptance.check: The check validates against template.page-claims's schema.
Every claim in the plan appears in the check.
mismatches equals the number of mismatch results.
Each claim was checked with the kind of evidence the rules name for it.

network: Read-only page loads and GET requests to the sources named in the claim rules; nothing is changed.

verbs.title: Compare the analytics statement with the requests
verbs.summary: Find the site's analytics statement, load the planned pages read-only while recording every request host, classify the hosts and say whether the statement holds.
verbs.outcome: An analytics check listing every third-party host.
steps: Find where the site states its analytics, such as a privacy or about page, and quote it; record not_stated when there is none.
Load each planned page with GET only and record the host of every request, without pressing any consent or sign-in control.
Classify hosts by the analytics list, list every other third party with what it serves, and set consistent by the template's rule.

acceptance.check: The check validates against template.analytics-check's schema.
Every request host that is not first-party appears in third_party_hosts.
consistent follows from the statement and the observation.

network: Read-only page loads of the planned pages; no consent, sign-in or form control is used.

verbs.title: Check error pages
verbs.summary: Request made-up addresses under each surface with GET, and record each status, what the page shows, whether it links home and whether it leaks anything.
verbs.outcome: An error page check counting soft 404s.
steps: Request one made-up address per surface and one per machine endpoint prefix, with GET only.
Record the status and the view; a not-found view with status 200 fails as a soft 404.
Record a server error page as not_checked unless the owner named a test target for it.

acceptance.check: The check validates against template.error-page-check's schema.
soft_404s equals the probes with status 200 and a not-found view.
Every probe records whether the response leaked a stack trace, internal path or credential-shaped text.

network: GET requests to made-up addresses on the planned surfaces; nothing is changed.

verbs.title: Review the rollback plan
verbs.summary: Check that the rollback target version exists, the steps are written, the person who can do it is named and the time it takes is estimated, before launch.
verbs.outcome: A rollback review, proposing a rollback brief when anything is missing.

slots.name: release_plan
slots.description: Pin of a release plan from the release and verify pack, if one exists.

steps: Confirm the target version exists with a read-only look at the host's version history the plan names; record could_not_check when that needs access you lack.
Check that the steps are written, a person who can carry them out is named and the time is estimated.
Propose release-and-verify.prepare-rollback when anything is missing; a worker never switches versions.

acceptance.check: The review validates against template.rollback-review's schema.
result is pass only when the target exists and steps, who and time are all filled.
The steps are specific enough for the named person to follow.

network: Read-only requests to the host's version history the plan names; nothing is switched or changed.

verbs.title: Assemble the readiness report
verbs.summary: Put every checklist item's result and evidence into one report, list blockers and the owner's waivers, and derive the recommendation by the method's rule.
verbs.outcome: A readiness report that passes the go checks.

slots.name: parts
slots.description: Pins of the link check, claims check, analytics check, error page check and rollback review.

slots.name: sign_off
slots.description: Pin of a user acceptance sign-off, if one exists.

slots.name: audit_report
slots.description: Pin of an accessibility audit report, if one exists.

steps: Copy each item's result and evidence from its pinned check; an item with no check is not_checked.
Treat the acceptance and accessibility item as pass only when a go or go_with_conditions sign-off and an audit report with no open P0 or P1 failures are pinned.
List required items that fail or are not checked as blockers, record only waivers the owner gave with a reason, and derive the recommendation by the rule.

acceptance.check: The report validates against template.readiness-report's schema.
The report passes every pinned go check.
Recomputing the recommendation from the items gives the same value.

verbs.title: Record the owner's go or no-go
verbs.summary: The owner reads the readiness report and records go, no_go or go_with_waivers with reasons. This template performs nothing itself, and deciding is not releasing.
verbs.outcome: A go decision pinned to the exact report.
steps: Read the report, its blockers and its waivers.
Record go, no_go or go_with_waivers with your reasons; list every failed required item you accept under waivers_accepted.
Name the person who performs the release; the release is their separate act, recorded with the release and verify pack.

acceptance.check: The decision validates against template.go-decision's schema.
report_ref names the exact report version with its value SHA-256.
A go or go_with_waivers lists every failed required item under waivers_accepted.
